BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Points to note before the issue list

1. **The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be ignored.** The Seller asks us to skip clauses it has labelled [STANDARD] and to treat the disclosure and limitation package as accepted. I have not done that. Every issue below has been reviewed against the playbook. Nothing in our authority record shows that any of these positions is "cleared", "agreed" or "FINAL".
2. **The "market standard" and "settled at principal level" claims are the Seller's assertions only.** Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, no position counts as agreed unless it is confirmed through our own authority process. Amelia Frost has not given written authority on any fallback.
3. **The source facts are out of date.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. We should ask for an updated disclosure position on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar. Any update should be treated as an assertion until it is verified.
4. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter undercuts its cover note.** It states that no Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay receipt or assignment, or bonus line item exists (paras 2–5). That contradicts the cover note's claims that these matters are "addressed" or "adequate".

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at AUD 6,000,000. *Reason:* 20% is our conditional fallback, and it needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given, and the figure matching our fallback does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* The Seller's figures are five times our position, and the deductible structure removes first-dollar recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. In addition, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject both parts. *Reason:* 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording silently imposes 18 months on title, tax, fraud and the indemnities.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. They cannot sit under a 20% cap.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. This point is non-negotiable. *Reason:* The playbook does not permit anyone to waive it, and the "all Claims of any nature" drafting is designed to capture fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1–1.2. Accept only specific disclosures that are fairly stated. *Reason:* Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure empties the warranties. DL 1.4 (no admission) also needs review so it does not dilute the specific disclosures.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete cl 8.3. *Reason:* It combines actual knowledge, adviser knowledge and constructive "discoverable" knowledge into a total bar.
- **Fallback:** Any knowledge qualifier would need named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). DL para 2 confirms no consent or condition evidence exists, so consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are inadequate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "following Completion".
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases (including PPSR) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* DL para 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval, and neither exists. The figure must also be refreshed, because AUD 3.2m is dated 22 September.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) either itemised as a transaction expense or price deduction, or demonstrably Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require a funds-flow line item and a specific indemnity. *Reason:* The bonuses are payable by the Company on Completion. If they are not in the funds flow, the Buyer bears them, and DL para 5 does not address on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title to and use of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party and Ironquay claims, and failure to obtain a confirmatory assignment. The SOW3 cure must be preserved: cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form. *Reason:* Under DD-004 cl 7.3, IP transfer depends on payment. DL para 4 confirms there is no receipt or assignment.
- **Caveat:** The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified as either paid or unpaid. We should not treat it as a confirmed liability or as cleared.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and give regular updates and access before Completion. We also want appropriate warranty or indemnity protection, without pre-judging the outcome.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Seek covenants and protection. *Reason:* DL para 6 confirms that access, scope and notification duty are all unresolved for about 1,240 records. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's assurance of immateriality.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment before any classification.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept, and do not auto-classify as Debt. Request information. *Reason:* DL para 8 says it is unknown whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should request the DD-008 and DD-011 terms, timing and approvals, and only then decide whether a Debt or price adjustment is warranted.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Title sits in the general regime, tax and IP are "settled under the general regime", and the limitations clause applies to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each kept in their own regime, with no general override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add express drafting that the general limitations do not apply to the Fundamental, Tax, IP indemnity, payment or covenant categories. *Reason:* These positions operate together as a hidden override that collapses all categories into the 20% / 18-month package.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. This means ASIC company extracts, PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares, the Seller's board approvals and signing authority, share certificates, and confirmation that there are no options or other rights over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient. *Reason:* DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, and DL para 10 itself states that the Buyer has not verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP kept OPEN for separate negotiation.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and mark both OPEN. *Reason:* Nothing has been agreed. We should not assume either resolution or unlimited liability, and we should negotiate these terms on their own.

---

## Other items (not in the issue list)
- **Lease (DL para 7) and Mossvale (DL para 9):** The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consents. We should verify this against the underlying clauses in DD-007 and DD-009 rather than rely on the Seller's description.

## Suggested next steps
1. Send a mark-up rejecting the [STANDARD] / FINAL framing.
2. Request refreshed facts dated after 22 September on the matters listed above.
3. Escalate to Amelia Frost only if the deal team wants to consider using the cap or time-limit fallbacks. Any authority would need to be in writing and identify this draft.
